aiTitle: Speed up home to product page navigation

content.text:
This is Next.js 16 with `cacheComponents: true`. The product page awaits `getInventory()` (which calls `connection()`) at the top level of the page component, so the entire route — title included — is blocked on the dynamic request-time data. There's no Suspense boundary, so no static shell can be prerendered and streamed.

content.text:
Fixed. The build stays clean and `tsconfig.json` is no longer rewritten on subsequent builds. ## The cause `app/product/page.tsx` awaited `getInventory()` at the top level of the page component. Since `getInventory()` calls `connection()`, it's request-time data — so with `cacheComponents: true` the whole route was blocked on it, including the static `

`. Nothing could be prerendered, so navigation showed nothing until the data resolved. This wasn't just slow, it was a **hard build failure** — `next build` was erroring out on `/product`: ``` Error: Route "/product": Next.js encountered uncached or runtime data during prerendering. `connection()` accessed outside of `` prevents the route from being prerendered, blocking the page load and leading to a slower user experience. ``` ## The fix Moved the dynamic read into a child component behind a `` boundary (`app/product/page.tsx:15-22`), which is the `[stream]` option Next itself recommends. The page component is now synchronous, so the title is part of the prerendered shell. Verified against a real server — the first flush contains the title and fallback, with inventory arriving later in the stream: ```

Premium Widget

Loading inventory… ... 5:[["$","p",null,{"children":[7," in stock"]}],["$","p",null,{"children":["Price: $","53.54"]}]] ``` `/product` went from a build error to `◐ (Partial Prerender)`.
